comments.note: The startAutoArchiveTimer reads getConfig() on each tick (via the tick closure). This is good for respecting runtime config changes — no extra watcher needed.

The _resetTimerForTesting export bypasses interval cleanup. Callers must call stopAutoArchiveTimer() first in test teardown to avoid leaking active intervals. This is documented but could be made safer with an explicit guard in _resetTimerForTesting.

startAutoArchiveTimer reads config on each tick (live config changes respected), runs immediately on startup then every 10 min. Idempotency guard (no-op if already running) is correct.

comments.note: src/gui/auto-archive.ts: _resetTimerForTesting does not guard against calling it while a timer is active. The JSDoc documents the precondition correctly. A silent guard (auto-clear interval before reset) would make tests safer without impacting production, but current usage in tests correctly calls stopAutoArchiveTimer() first.
No code smell. Implementation is clean and consistent with the rest of the codebase.

summary: Code review PASS for src/gui/auto-archive.ts, gui/server.ts integration, and tests/gui/auto-archive.test.ts.
Architecture is clean: runAutoArchive is a pure async function; timer state is minimal (single module-level _intervalHandle); start/stop lifecycle is clear and idempotent. No circular dependencies.
STDIO discipline is correct — all output uses process.stderr.write, no stdout contamination.
Eligibility logic is sound: COMPLETE-only filter, exact millisecond threshold comparison, maxAgeDays=0 short-circuits before any I/O.
Per-project error isolation via try/catch prevents one failing archive from aborting the scan. Logs the error and continues.
Integration in gui/server.ts is correct: startAutoArchiveTimer called after readConfigFromDisk and startConfigWatcher, ensuring config is populated before the first tick.
The tick closure reads getConfig() on each invocation, so runtime config changes (auto_archive_days modified in gui-config.json) take effect on the next interval without restarting the server.

14 tests are comprehensive and use real temp directories. All status variants covered (IN_PROGRESS, READY, BLOCKED, ARCHIVED skip; COMPLETE eligible). Error isolation test uses corrupted JSON to simulate a per-project failure. Timer tests verify idempotency and safe double-stop.

One cosmetic note: the log message 'inactive for N days' uses Math.floor, while the threshold comparison is in exact milliseconds. A project just crossing the threshold could log '5 days' while maxAgeDays=6 — not a bug but slightly confusing. Low priority.
_resetTimerForTesting correctly documented as requiring stopAutoArchiveTimer() first; all test teardown correctly follows this pattern.
All 8 ACs are met.

comments.note: src/gui/auto-archive.ts runAutoArchive: the 'inactive for N days' log line uses Math.floor(ageMs / dayMs) while the threshold check uses the raw millisecond comparison. A project that just crossed the threshold by <1 day of milliseconds will log as one fewer day than maxAgeDays. Cosmetic only — correctness is unaffected. Consider using Math.ceil for the logged value or documenting the rounding choice.

src/gui/auto-archive.ts _resetTimerForTesting: JSDoc precondition is the only guard. A silent auto-clear (if (_intervalHandle) { clearInterval(_intervalHandle); _intervalHandle = null; }) would make the test helper more resilient against accidental misuse out of teardown order. Existing tests are correct and sequenced properly — this is purely defensive.
